entries.subject: Placement
entries.finding: Gaia DR3 source 6764026419748892160: position at J2016.0. Distance: Gaia DR3 parallax 14.7691 +/- 0.2115 mas (same row, RUWE 11.99): 67.71 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published. Proper motion: Gaia DR3 (same row): 21.447, -48.196 mas/yr. Radial velocity from SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 6764026419748892160 (quality A), from 2021MNRAS.506..150B; Gaia DR3 measures none.

entries.subject: Radius, mass and temperature
entries.finding: Radius 1.37 solar radii from Folsom et al., arXiv:1601.00684, Table 2: radius 1.37 solar radii (https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00684). Mass 1.17 solar masses from Folsom et al., arXiv:1601.00684, Table 2: mass 1.17 solar masses (https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00684). Temperature 4600 K from Pecaut & Mamajek (2013, ApJS 208, 9), the online table's version 2022.04.16, row K4V, for SIMBAD's spectral type K4V(e): Teff.

entries.subject: Color
entries.finding: A Planck spectrum at 4,600 K, because no archive holds a spectrum of this star (stis-ngsl: no HD number in SIMBAD; gaia-xp: Gaia DR3 published no sampled BP/RP spectrum of it; pulkovo: no HR number; kiehling: no HR number; kharitonov: no HR number; burnashev: no HR (BS) number), through the CIE 1931 2-degree observer: #ffdfc0. Routes tried in order: stis-ngsl: no HD number in SIMBAD; gaia-xp: Gaia DR3 published no sampled BP/RP spectrum of it; pulkovo: no HR number; kiehling: no HR number; kharitonov: no HR number; burnashev: no HR (BS) number; planck: used.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 4,600 K and log g 4.23 (u1 0.763, u2 0.033): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used.

entries.subject: Spin
entries.finding: Inclination 68 degrees from the line of sight, period 5.7 d, from Folsom et al., arXiv:1601.00684, Table 2: rotation period 5.7 d and an axis 68 degrees from the line of sight, the values its magnetic maps were made with; the axis's direction on the sky is a convention.
